QD3-001 answered and read (J: yes to both; on writing, the rulings file gives a decision and a reason for every id, with no default decision). What rested on my assumption: every ruling so far went through mem.py adjudicate and stands as written; the reads were through the verbs, so R01's instantiate lines (packets one to three) were read with how clipped at 90 characters, plus the seeded concept draws and the concept reads named in each reason. I now build the whole-line reader (out/_analysis/d3_packet.py) and the batch writer (out/_analysis/d3_adjudicate_batch.py), re-read R01's ruled packets whole through the reader and re-rule any line its whole text overturns, and use both for the rest of the census.

adjudicated belgium-001: reject (re-ruled on the whole-line re-read: c0001 adds a pole to a flag already on the canvas, c0003 contributes while others deface it, c0005 works on a figure beside it and c0037 calls for an outline; building and design talk on an existing flag (P03, P02), not proposing, mapping or beginning the mark)

D3a-01, the revisit after QD3-001: R01's ruled instantiate lines (0 to 248 in op order) re-read whole through d3_packet.py; every ruling stood except belgium-001, re-ruled to reject (its concepts show a member adding to and repairing a flag already on the canvas, not a start). Three thin concepts read in full confirmed their rulings (GabrielDropout c0067, MiamiHurricanes c0030, SwissNeutralityZone c0085: each the member's own account of starting). From here R01's lines are read whole and written per packet through d3_adjudicate_batch.py from a rulings file, each id with its own decision and reason. Slip: the guard refused cut -c after the helper once; rerun without it.
